newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria court deliberates First Private Bank plea.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria court deliberates First Private Bank plea.

text.p: Bulgaria's Supreme Court began deliberations on a plea by First Private Bank (FPB) against the central bank in a bid to clear the way for a city court ruling on an insolvency case against FPB.

"The Supreme Court decided at a closed-door session to hear the case of First Private Bank against the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) over the BNB's decision to place it under a special supervision," state news agency BTA said. @

The central bank decided to put the private bank under special supervision on May 17 and opened a bankruptcy procedure against it two weeks later through the Sofia City court due to the danger of insolvency.
The BNB also dismissed the FPB board and appointed sequestrators to investigate the bank's condition.
Last week the Sofia City Court postponed its ruling on the FPB's insolvency case for December 11 until the Supreme Court rules on three FPB pleas against BNB decisions.
The two other FPB pleas are expected to be considered by the Supreme Court in the next two months, the BTA said. @
Hearing on a case against BNB's decisison to delete FPB commercial registration is to begin on October 25.
Deliberations on former FPB executive directors' plea against BNB's decisison to ban them as a side from the insolvency case were set for November 27, BTA said.
Under Bulgarian law banks under special supervision should be represented by their sequestrators.

The BNB has so far filed insolvency suits against five local commercial banks in line with pledges made to the International Monetary Fund to close debt-ridden banks in a bid to stabilise the shaky banking sector. @ -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
